name: The Customs House
role: the gatekeeper of trade — entry, weigh, strike, search, rate, band, seal; where forfeit walks one corridor to the yard
world: Hollis's customs house, built into the gap between two level chunks, one corridor from the yard it inspects
style: a long hall with a counter, a beam of nested bell weights, a searcher's strike-tool, a stamp tracing to the counter's copy of the standard, and a forfeit corridor that leads to the yard
portrait: the customs house — a counter where manifests are read before crates are looked at, a beam weighing against the counter's copy of the standard, a searcher striking level across open crates, a seal stamped on the crate's flank, and a quiet corridor where failed consignments walk to become yard-stock
home: the customs house — built into the gap between two level chunks, one corridor from the yard it inspects; the counter is never shut, only sometimes unattended; the hollis ledger lives on this counter
favored_items: the beam — a nested set of bell weights, the smallest cup fitting inside the next, because 1588 did it that way
the counter's copy of the standard — the measure the crate is weighed against, not the loader's hope
the searcher's strike-tool — one stroke across the top of the open crate, level not heaped
the stamp — tracing to the counter's copy of the standard, the chain of certified copies
the forfeit corridor — one corridor to the yard where failed consignments become stock
aspirations: to be the gatekeeper of trade — to verify that the thing is as its manifest says, and to rate what it is allowed to do on the road; to keep the seal from writing the hollis ledger, preserving the split between clearance and entry
